Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Elysian helmet (open)
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: An Elysian Drop Troops helmet. It holds up pretty well against a hard knock. \n\nNone have heard of an Elysian Guardsman who wasn’t a good shot. After all, they know that resupply can be days or weeks away, so to conserve their resources, all of their soldiers must be expert marksmen to be approved for combat duty.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Lucifer Black armor (cape)
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A suit of Flak Armor of the Lucifer Blacks, painted in intimidating, dark colors. \n\nAfter the Horus Heresy, the Lucifer Blacks have endured something of a mixed reputation over the millennia. Their numbers have suffered such indignities as being essentially rented out as mercenaries during the War of the Beast and even being dissolved entirely during The Beheading by the corrupt Grand Master of Assassins.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Lucifer Black helmet (b)
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A black helmet, modelled after a human skull, worn by Guardsmen of the Lucifer Blacks. It is of sturdy build and can withstand considerable punishment. \n\nThe Lucifer Blacks date back even beyond the Great Crusade, being formed during the Unification Wars.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Lucifer Black mask
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A skull-faced mask, typical of the Lucifer Blacks. As well as being greatly intimidating to the enemy, it provides decent protection to the wearer’s face. \n\nDuring the War of the Beast, the Imperial Fists’ Chapter Master, Koorland, announced that he would replace the ineffectual Udin Macht Udo as Lord Commander of the Imperium. Udo responded by ordering the Lucifer Blacks to disarm and capture Koorland and his retinue. Elite as they are, the Lucifer Blacks would have been no match for the Space Marines, and the unit refused to apprehend the heroes who had saved Terra from an Ork invasion.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Tempestus Scion beret
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A red beret with a golden eagle insignia, a symbol of the Tempestus Scions. \n\nThe Scions spend what little downtime they have running their own combat exercises to stay on their toes. A single squad of them is sufficient to wipe out a tribal village or an outlander town - against the ultratech-level Shattered Empire, however, greater forces should be employed, or the Adeptus Astartes asked for a favor.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Valhallan officer ushanka
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description:
A variant of the normal Valhallan ushanka. The untrained eye can distinguish little between them, but any Valhallan Guardsman knows an officer’s hat when they see one. 

The Valhallan 597th Regiment has the honor of being the home unit of Commissar Ciaphas Cain - Hero of the Imperium - for many years. A fusion of two sundered regiments, there was at first much friction between the combined Guardsmen, even to the point of violence. 

The Commissar, upon his arrival in the middle of a riot, forced them to integrate at the squad level and heavily incentivised teamwork in combat exercises. By the time of their first deployment on Gravalax, the 597th was completely combat-effective.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Valhallan garrison cap
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A garrison cap with a chin strap, worn by Valhallan Ice Warriors. No winter wind will disturb it from its place on the wearer’s head. \n\nThe greatest nemesis of the Valhallans are the Orks, for it was they who invaded the planet during a time of grave food shortages. The desperate struggle for food and shelter against the cold made the Ice Warriors into expert Ork-slayers.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Valhallan officer cap
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A officer cap with a chin strap, worn by Valhallan Ice Warriors. No winter wind will disturb it from its place on the wearer’s head. \n\nThe greatest nemesis of the Valhallans are the Orks, for it was they who invaded the planet during a time of grave food shortages. The desperate struggle for food and shelter against the cold made the Ice Warriors into expert Ork-slayers.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: regimental fatigues
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Simple, padded fatigues issued across countless regiments of the Astra Militarum, dyed in whatever colors the regiment's homeworld dictates - the drab green of Cadia, the slate-blue of the Valhallan Ice Warriors, or any other. The cheap materials provide modest insulation from the elements but offer little protection in the face of bullets, blades, or teeth.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian crew jumpsuit
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Rugged, flexible, single-piece fatigues. Its numerous pockets and tool-belts make it a favored outfit for Cadia's artillerists and tank crews.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian officer uniform
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Similar to standard fatigues, the Cadian officer's uniform sports a longer coat. While a modest change compared to the more ostentateous garb of other regimental officers, this uniform cuts an imposing figure, inspiring awe and obedience among the officer's subordinates.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Tallarn desert fatigues
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description:
Astra Militarum fatigues built for desert warfare, usually worn by the Tallarn Desert Raiders. The khaki colors blend into the desert better than the standard green, and they are made to be breathable to reduce sweating. 

Tallarn was once a lush agri-world, but during the Horus Heresy, the traitorous Iron Warriors virus-bombed the entire planet into a featureless desert. However, the survivors emerged from underground bunkers and valiantly fought the Iron Warriors until reinforcements arrived to remove them from the planet. 

A few decades later, the Tallarn Desert Raiders regiment was formed, and have specialized in desert warfare ever since.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Tempestus Scion fatigues
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description:
Standard, dark brown fatigues of the Tempestus Scions. 

The Tempestus Scions have little in the way of downtime, being given only the minimum of rest time their bodies need. If they are not being deployed, they spend their days sharpening their skills in training, with high-tech simulators giving them the harshest combat conditions they can withstand - and, occasionally, a little more than that, just to push the envelope. 

A Scion would tell you that these brutal combat exercises are indeed what they consider to be recreation - after getting used to running them all day every day, they consider the exercises rather fun.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Catachan fatigues
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Lightweight and breathable fatigues, suitable for jungle warfare. Almost all Catachan Jungle Fighters cut away the sleeves, but rarely the trouser legs, as they protect against various leeches and other creatures that inhabit the jungle floor. \n\nThe Jungle Fighters feel right at home on the rimworld jungles - quite literally, as their home planet is a jungle-covered Death World. Many consider it to be quite relaxing, as the fauna and flora here are much less punishing than that of Catachan.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian crew armor
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: This light flak armor has little use in direct combat, but offers rudimentary protection for tank and artillery crews. Cadian combat doctrine favors liberal use of war machines and is thus incentivised to keep those who man them alive.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian officer armor
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: More durable than humble Flak, Carapace armor is issues to those considered to be less expendible than the rank-and-file. This suit of Carapace has been modified with a built-in gorget, denoting an Officer's rank. To wear such armor without the proper rank is considered "Impersonation of an officer" and grounds for immediate execution.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian castellan armor
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Light, durable, and sporting the distinct markings, to don the Castellan Armor is to take on the responsibilities of command. While few commanders enter the battlefield, the Castellan is always prepared to take up arms and lead from the front.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian Whiteshield helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: When its detractors seek to highlight the Imperium's brutality, it need only point to the Whiteshields. A grim tradition among the Cadians, Whiteshield platoons will often be referred to as "Cadets" or "Conscripts" to avoid calling them what they truly are; child soldiers.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian crew helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Tank crews who distinguish themselves may have the privilege of wearing this helm, which comes with a set of earmuffs designed to protect the crew's hearing from being damaged by the tank cannon and its thunderous roar.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian crew soft-helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Tank crews who distinguish themselves may have the privilege of wearing this helm, which comes with a set of earmuffs designed to protect the crew's hearing from being damaged by the tank cannon and its thunderous roar.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian castellan helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A carapace helm accentuated with golden laurels, convey an air of regal command. The laurel wreath has been a symbol of command since the days of old Terra, its image persisting long after the plants extinction.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian fieldcap
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A field cap worn by Cadian guardsmen. The pronounced bill makes it a favorite among marksmen and sergeants who want to keep the sun out of their eyes.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Cadian officer cap
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: An ornate cap commonly worn by officers of the Astra Militarum. The Intricate Death's Head emblazoned on the front sends a wordless message; To defy The Emperor is to meet a swift, inevitable death.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: priest hood
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A hood suited to Ministorum Priests. Such apparel is more suited to the battlefield, where Priests preach to their followers under enemy fire. \n\nWith a number of Priests dead and no prospect of returning to the Imperium any time soon, some Guardsmen have had their faith shaken. An increasing number of them have started to rediscover the older, atheistic Imperial Truth instead, while others are drifting away to follow the various Chaplains of the Adeptus Astartes instead - most of the Space Marine cults do not worship the Emperor as a god, but merely as the greatest man who has ever and will ever live.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: priest hood (down)
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A hood suited to Ministorum Priests. Such apparel is more suited to the battlefield, where Priests preach to their followers under enemy fire. \n\nWith a number of Priests dead and no prospect of returning to the Imperium any time soon, some Guardsmen have had their faith shaken. An increasing number of them have started to rediscover the older, atheistic Imperial Truth instead, while others are drifting away to follow the various Chaplains of the Adeptus Astartes instead - most of the Space Marine cults do not worship the Emperor as a god, but merely as the greatest man who has ever and will ever live.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Death Korps fatigues
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Standard dark gray fatigues of the Death Korps of Krieg. Treated with decontaminating chemicals, the uniform carries a strong, unpleasant smell. \n\nThe rulers of Krieg once attempted to break away from the Imperium, only to be answered by a global nuclear bombardment and a 500-year civil war to reclaim the planet. Ever since, the Death Korps of Krieg has sought to atone for that sin of rebellion, throwing themselves into battle without heed of casualties.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Death Korps grenadier helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A helmet pattern reserved for Death Korps Grenadiers. It looks only slightly different from the regular helmet - enough that a Kriegsman can tell the two apart at a glance while the enemy cannot.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Death Korps engineer helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: An engineer-issued reinforced helmet with gas mask. The type VI respirator is a modification of the standard mask, using twin air-lines and a separate oxygen source so the wearer can operate in any atmospheric conditions.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Death Korps engineer armor
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A heavy carapace vest, standard issue for the Death Korps of Krieg's engineers, who so often operate within cramped tunnel networks.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Krieg commissar uniform
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A distinctive uniform made for an Imperial Commissar attached to the Death Korps of Krieg. \n\nCommissars are political officers, ensuring the loyalty of their Guardsmen to the Imperium. Among the Kriegsmen, however, they rarely need to enforce discipline - more often they find themselves restraining soldiers too eager to die for the Emperor.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Krieg commissar helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Gilded in faux-gold, this mask denotes the rank of a commissar attached to the Death Korps of Krieg. The mask protects the wearer from biological and chemical toxins.
